one_line: Fresh pale sand/silt lobe deposited at a wadi-fan apex in late Aug 2025 (flood splay or wind-blown sand); no structure in any image.
summary: before.png and after.png (Sentinel-2, Sep-Oct 2024 vs Sep 2025) show the same pale sand tongue at the head of a south-draining wadi fan between dark sandstone outcrops; after onset the tongue is marginally brighter with no new edge, object or shadow, and difference.png shows a soft brightening of +0.02 to +0.04 in the north of the box feathering into a fan-wide +0.01 to +0.02, with NDVI flat. hires.png (Esri, acquired 2023-09-09, pre-change) and all six wayback_strip.png releases (2014 to 2026-05-28, the last identical to the 2023 picture) show only braided wash channels and bare sand, nothing built. The per-scene series in dossier.json confirms the step: inside-minus-ring NBR contrast 0.034-0.052 for the 17 good scenes to 2025-08-06 (the 0.067 point on 2025-01-28 is an S2C scene read without its radiometric offset), then 0.011-0.021 for all 13 scenes from 2025-09-05 to 2026-11-24, with brightness contrast rising from about 0.026 to 0.033. All three sceptics refuted the candidate and converged on one cause: a lobe of fresh pale sediment at the gully mouth, whose change vector matches the bright-sand-minus-dark-rock endmember (cosine 0.978), whose 10 m shape is a soft teardrop with a tail down the wash rather than the rectangle implied by the 20 m bounding-box metrics (footprint_source 'bbox', about 10x7 pixels), which appeared in a single step between the 26 and 31 August 2025 passes while the 31 August scene shows a basin-wide wet-ground/cloud transient, and which has a same-vector sibling (OC0047) 8.8 km away in the same season. SAR (-0.30 dB, noise 0.23) and thermal (-0.55 K, noise 0.63) did not change, as expected for a thin sediment sheet and not for a built object, so the panel records an ordinary sediment deposit; whether a flash flood or wind delivered it is not resolved and does not need to be.
explanation: Fresh pale sand/silt deposited as a lobe at the apex of a sand-filled wadi fan on the Gilf Kebir margin between 26 and 31 August 2025, most likely a flash-flood splay from the feeder gully to the north (the 31 Aug Sentinel-2 scene shows a basin-wide wetting/cloud transient), with wind-blown sand as the alternative delivery; the 'installation' shape signature comes from bounding-box metrics on a 10x7 pixel blob at 20 m, not from the changed pixels.
next_step: A sub-metre image acquired after 5 September 2025 of 23.1937 N 26.0002 E (Maxar, Planet SkySat, or an Esri Wayback release with a post-2025 acquisition date; the 2026-05-28 release still shows the 2023 picture): a smooth sediment lobe or fresh sand ripples at the gully mouth with no tracks confirms deposition, while tracks, a graded pad or pits would reopen it. Secondary: IMERG or CHIRPS daily rainfall for 26-31 Aug 2025 at 23.2 N 26.0 E to confirm the storm, and fix the earthsearch:boa_offset_applied handling that corrupted the 2025-01-28 S2C scene in the series.
